arxiv-2209-12912.title: A detailed star formation history for the extremely diffuse Andromeda XIX dwarf galaxy 2020 A detailed star formation history for the extremely diffuse Andromeda XIX dwarf galaxy – 3
arxiv-2209-12912.creator: Michelle L. M. Collins, Benjamin F. Williams, Erik J. Tollerud, Eduardo Balbinot, Karoline M. Gilbert, Andrew Dolphin
arxiv-2209-12912.description: Abstract We present deep imaging of the ultra-diffuse Andromeda XIX dwarf galaxy from the Advance Camera for Surveys on the Hubble Space Telescope which resolves its stellar populations to below the oldest main sequence turn-off. We derive a full star formation history for the galaxy using MATCH, and find no evidence of star formation in the past 8 Gyr.

arxiv-2312-01153.creator: ​, Roberto Ruiz de Austri
arxiv-2312-01153.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by ​, Roberto Ruiz de Austri. The energy spectra of particles produced from dark matter (DM) annihilation or decay are one of the fundamental ingredients to calculate the predicted fluxes of cosmic rays and radiation searched for in indirect DM detection.

arxiv-2401-01521.title: Quantum Leak: Timing Side-Channel Attacks on Cloud-Based Quantum Services
arxiv-2401-01521.creator: Chao Lu † , Esha Telang ‡ , Aydin Aysu ‡ , Kanad Basu †
arxiv-2401-01521.description: Abstract Quantum computing offers significant acceleration capabilities over its classical counterpart in various application domains. Consequently, there has been substantial focus on improving quantum computing capabilities. However, to date, the security implications of these quantum computing platforms have been largely overlooked.

arxiv-2404-11406.title: Pharmacokinetic Measurements in Dose Finding Model Guided by Escalation with Overdose Control
arxiv-2404-11406.creator: Arnab Kumar Maity, Satrajit Roy Chowdhury, Ray Li, Lada Markovtsova, Roberto Bugarini
arxiv-2404-11406.description: Abstract Oncology drug development starts with a dose escalation phase to find the maximal tolerable dose (MTD). Dose limiting toxicity (DLT) is the primary endpoint for dose escalation phase. Traditionally, model-based dose escalation trial designs recommend a dose for escalation based on an assumed dose-DLT relationship.

arxiv-2408-15693.title: Synthetic Forehead-creases Biometric Generation for Reliable User Verification
arxiv-2408-15693.creator: Abhishek Tandon, Geetanjali Sharma, Gaurav Jaswal, Aditya Nigam, Raghavendra Ramachandra
arxiv-2408-15693.description: Abstract Recent studies have emphasized the potential of forehead-crease patterns as an alternative for face, iris, and periocular recognition, presenting contactless and convenient solutions, particularly in situations where faces are covered by surgical masks. However, collecting forehead data presents challenges, including cost and time constraints, as developing and optimizing forehead verification methods requires a substantial number of high-quality images.

arxiv-2409-04324.title: Geometrical Approach to Logical Qubit Fidelities of Neutral Atom CSS Codes
arxiv-2409-04324.creator: J.J. Postema, S.J.J.M.F. Kokkelmans
arxiv-2409-04324.description: Abstract Encoding quantum information in a quantum error correction (QEC) code enhances protection against errors. Imperfection of quantum devices due to decoherence effects will limit the fidelity of quantum gate operations. In particular, neutral atom quantum computers will suffer from correlated errors because of the finite lifetime of the Rydberg states that facilitate entanglement.

arxiv-2502-18644.title: Steered Generation via Gradient Descent on Sparse Features
arxiv-2502-18644.creator: Sumanta Bhattacharyya, Pedram Rooshenas
arxiv-2502-18644.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) encode a diverse range of linguistic features within their latent representations, which can be harnessed to steer their output toward specific target characteristics. In this paper, we modify the internal structure of LLMs by training sparse autoencoders to learn a sparse representation of the query embedding, allowing precise control over the model’s attention distribution.

arxiv-2504-16554.title: Temperature switchable self-propulsion activity of liquid crystalline microdroplets
arxiv-2504-16554.creator: Manoj Kumar, Siddharth Sane, Aniruddh Murali, Shashi Thutupalli
arxiv-2504-16554.description: Abstract We report on a switchable emulsion droplet microswimmer by utilizing a temperature-dependent transition of the droplet phase. The droplets, made from a liquid crystalline (LC) smectic phase material ( T = T= 25 ∘ C), self-propel only in their nematic and isotropic phases at elevated temperatures ( T ≥ T\geq 33.5 ∘ C).

arxiv-2510-14151.title: Privacy-Preserving and Incentive-Driven Relay-Based Framework for Cross-Domain Blockchain Interoperability
arxiv-2510-14151.creator: Saeed Moradi 1 , Koosha Esmaeilzadeh Khorasani 1 , Sara Rouhani 1 2
arxiv-2510-14151.description: Abstract Interoperability is essential for transforming blockchains from isolated networks into collaborative ecosystems, unlocking their full potential. While significant progress has been made in public blockchain interoperability, bridging permissioned and permissionless blockchains poses unique challenges due to differences in access control, architectures, and security requirements. This paper introduces a blockchain-agnostic framework to enable interoperability between permissioned and permissionless networks.

pmc-12430665.title: Cucurbitacin B from Cucurbitaceae Plants: Treating Pancreatic Cancer via Inducing Mitophagy, Inhibiting Glycolysis, and Enhancing Immune Function

pmc-13006522.title: MOS is a key regulator of meiotic midbody assembly and prevents abnormal divisions in mouse eggs and their polar bodies
pmc-13006522.creator: Gisela Cairo, Muhammad A Haseeb, Zachary Boyce Joy, Karen Schindler, Soni Lacefield
pmc-13006522.description: Mammalian female meiosis is uniquely regulated to produce a developmentally competent egg capable of supporting embryogenesis. During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes segregate, with half extruded into the first polar body. The egg then arrests at metaphase II and only resumes meiosis and extrudes the second polar body following fertilization.

pmc-13085286.title: Linking genomic variation in Spiroplasma endosymbionts to male production and male-killing in the pea aphid
pmc-13085286.creator: Hiroshi Arai, Lucas Bodelle, Frédérique Mahéo, Romuald Cloteau, Gaëtan Denis, Ryuichi Koga, Daisuke Kageyama, Akiko Sugio, Jean-Christophe Simon
pmc-13085286.description: BackgroundEndosymbiotic bacteria of the genus Spiroplasma (Mollicutes) are widespread among arthropods and plants with some lineages inducing male killing in several insect hosts. In the pea aphid, Acyrthosiphon pisum, three divergent clades of Spiroplasma ixodetis have been described, but male killing has been so far reported in only one clade.

pmc-13152375.title: Small airways disease is common in mild COPD and symptomatic subjects at risk with normal spirometry: baseline data from CAPTO-COPD
pmc-13152375.creator: Frederik Trinkmann, Mustafa Abdo, Felix J.F. Herth, Klaus F. Rabe, Anne-Marie Kirsten, Henrik Watz
pmc-13152375.description: BackgroundCurrent guideline-based diagnosis of airflow limitation in COPD focuses on spirometry, which is insensitive to early small airway changes of symptomatic smokers or subjects at risk. Therefore, we sought to determine the frequency of small airways disease (SAD) in these groups compared with mild COPD, and evaluate associations with symptoms as well as health-related quality of life (HRQoL).

pmc-13236978.title: Braking Parkinson’s progression: the hypothetical druggable role of striatal parvalbumin interneurons
pmc-13236978.creator: Quansheng He, Xuan Wang, Xiaowen Zhang, Yousheng Shu
pmc-13236978.description: The striatum is one of the first brain regions affected in Parkinson’s disease (PD), where dopaminergic axons projecting from the substantia nigra undergo dying-back degeneration. Growing evidence shows that dopamine depletion triggers network-level remodeling in the striatum, whose pathological significance extends far beyond acute changes in neuronal excitability.

pmc-13242670.title: Blood-based DNA methylation marker model for short-term and long-term lung cancer risk prediction
pmc-13242670.creator: Megha Bhardwaj, Yi-Qian Sun, Clara Frick, Ben Schöttker, Oluf Dimitri Røe, Bernd Holleczek, Xiao-Mei Mai, Hermann Brenner
pmc-13242670.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundScreening heavy smokers with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) has been shown to reduce lung cancer (LC) mortality, however, identifying the specific high-risk population that benefits most, a critical requirement for implementing effective and cost-efficient screening, remains challenging.MethodsWe developed and validated a blood-based DNA methylation marker model (BBDMM) for all participants, including both ever and never smokers, using the LC risk-informative CpG sites from epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS).

pmc-13399178.title: Computed tomography reveals multiple origins of extreme caudal vertebral pneumaticity in sauropod dinosaurs
pmc-13399178.creator: Samantha L. Beeston, Daniela Schwarz, Paul Upchurch, Stephen F. Poropat, Patrick Asbach, Philip D. Mannion
pmc-13399178.description: Postcranial skeletal pneumaticity (PSP) is common in the presacral vertebrae of sauropod dinosaurs, but seemingly rare in their caudal vertebrae. Where identified, evidence for caudal vertebral PSP in sauropods is primarily based on the presence of external features, such as lateral fossae.

pmc-13486892.title: Global land-use change rivals climate change in driving projected diversity shifts of terrestrial vertebrates
pmc-13486892.creator: Xiaojuan Liu, Bingqi Xie, Wei Tu, Yang Wu, Minyi Gao, Nan Xu, Xia Li
pmc-13486892.description: SummaryGlobal biodiversity is declining at an unprecedented rate under the combined pressures of climate and land-use change, yet their relative contributions and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we developed a filtering-energy-stress framework to characterize multidimensional land-use change and integrate it, together with climate change, into species distribution models for projecting future biodiversity dynamics under shared socio-economic pathways (SSPs).

pmc-13641338.title: Ultrasound Characteristics of Twisted Pedunculated Subserosal Uterine Leiomyomas: A Case Report and a Systematic Review of the Literature
pmc-13641338.creator: Maddalena Paoli, Pietro Pasquini, Alessandra Pennetta, Ghizzi Chiara, Maria Cristina Scifo, Evaldo Giacomucci
pmc-13641338.description: Torsion of pedunculated subserosal uterine leiomyomas (TPSUL) is a rare but potentially severe condition that may require emergency surgery. This article aims to summarize the existing literature by presenting a systematic review and an illustrative case report. A total of 38 articles describing 42 cases of TPSUL were analyzed to identify recurring ultrasound features that may aid in preoperative diagnosis.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Records.— The corporation shall keep— (1) correct and complete records of account; (2) minutes of the proceedings of its members, board of directors, and committees having any of the authority of its board of directors.
